title: TileLang: Bridge Programmability and Performance in Modern Neural Kernels
claim: Ours reaches near-best speedup with far less code, escaping the usual tradeoff between performance and implementation simplicity.
layout: 1 scatter plot, log y-axis, color-gradient background, labeled speedup annotations
description: A single scatter plot titled 'MLA Performance and Code Complexity on H100'. The x-axis is code lines (LOC), from 0 to about 500. The y-axis is speedup normalized to PyTorch on a log scale, from 10^0 to 10^3. Four methods appear as colored markers with error bars, identified in a legend at lower right. TileLang is a blue circle at about 70 LOC and 841x. PyTorch is an orange triangle at the origin, about 15 LOC and 1.00x. Triton is a green square at about 140 LOC and 151x, with a large error bar. FlashMLA is a red diamond at about 480 LOC and 1040x. Each point has a speedup label in its own color. The background shades from green at top-left to pink-red at bottom-right, marking the desirable and undesirable regions. The eye goes first to the blue TileLang point in the top-left.
caption: Performance vs. code size trade-off for MLA kernels on NVIDIA H100. Points closer to the top-left indicate better balance between performance and implementation simplicity. The annotated speedup values indicate performance gains over the PyTorch implementation.
abstract: Modern AI algorithms increasingly adopt fused kernels for performance, but implementing them remains complex due to the lack of fine-grained control in existing compilers like Triton. We introduce TileLang, a controllable programming system for fused neural kernels. TileLang provides explicit tile-level primitives for memory placement, data movement, and parallel scheduling. To guide developers in hardware-aware programming, the TileLang introduces two key techniques: tile inference which models tile programs as fused graphs and automatically deduces tile configuration from partial annotations; and tile recommendation that suggests efficient tile configurations based on hardware profiles and heuristics. TileLang makes it easy to express a wide range of fused attention kernels in under 80 lines of Python code, reducing code size by up to 90% compared to manual implementations. Evaluations show that TileLang achieves up to 5x speedup over Triton on NVIDIA H100 and up to 6 on AMD GPUs, demonstrating its ability to bridge programmability and performance.
